hints.title: Separate the finite sum
hints.body: Integration distributes over a finite sum. Consider the area under each graph y=f(2r−1x) on the stated interval before adding the contributions.
hints.recap: An integral of a finite sum is the sum of the separate integrals.
hints.pitfall: The exponent acts inside the input of the function; it does not multiply the output.
hints.pause: Sketch the first term and calculate its area on the interval.

recall.reminder: An integral of a finite sum is the sum of the separate integrals.

hints.title: Track horizontal compression
hints.body: Replacing x by kx compresses the graph horizontally by factor 1/k. Keep its heights unchanged and examine how many complete triangular pieces fit between the stated limits.
hints.recap: Horizontal scaling changes the widths of graph features while preserving their heights.
hints.pitfall: Account for both the narrower pieces and how many now lie inside the fixed interval.
hints.pause: Sketch the next two scaled graphs and calculate their areas geometrically.

recall.reminder: Horizontal scaling changes the widths of graph features while preserving their heights.

hints.title: Generalise the area calculation
hints.body: For the remaining powers of two, count the full triangles in the interval and multiply by the area of one triangle. Then return to the finite sum.
hints.recap: Add the definite areas of the separate pieces over the stated interval.
hints.pitfall: Treat the unscaled first term carefully rather than assuming that it contains a whole period.
hints.pause: Derive each contribution from its number and width of pieces, then add all the terms required.

recall.reminder: Add the definite areas of the separate pieces over the stated interval.

solution:
1. Integrate term by term. We need ∑r=110∫01f(2r−1x)dx. For r=1, the graph on [0,1] is a rising line from height 0 to height 1, so its area is 12.

2. Scale the triangular wave. For k=2r−1 with r≥2, k is a positive even integer. The graph f(kx) has period 2/k and contains k/2 complete triangles on [0,1]. Each triangle has base 2/k and height 1, hence area 1/k.

3. Add the contributions. Each scaled term therefore has integral (k/2)(1/k)=12. There are ten terms, so the total is 10×12=5.

Answer C. The extra triangles exactly compensate for their narrower bases.
knowledgePattern: Use horizontal compression and repeated triangular areas to integrate a finite sum
